title: Defeat of Tikal in the "star war" of 562 CE
summary: Caracol Altar 21, dedicated in AD 633, records a "star war" defeat of Tikal in AD 562. The attacker's name is damaged; Simon Martin doubts it was Caracol's king and favours the Snake (Kaan) kingdom. The defeat coincides with the start of a roughly 130-year gap in Tikal monument dedications.

uncertainty.note: Sources give AD 562. A Long Count equivalent (searches suggest 9.6.8.4.2 or 9.6.7.16.2) was not confirmed on any opened page and is omitted.

as_recorded.calendar: Gregorian (AD); Long Count not given on opened pages
as_recorded.value: the defeat of Tikal that took place in AD 562

importance.justification: A pivotal Classic Maya defeat, marking the start of the Tikal Hiatus.

sources.title: Caracol Altar 21 Revisited (Simon Martin, PARI Journal 6:1)
A Caracol Emblem Glyph at Tikal

reviewer_note: The victor is unresolved (Martin: unknown; the Snake kingdom is a candidate, Caracol's king is discounted). Long Count requested but unconfirmed, so absent. Tikal ruler's fate is not stated in the sources I opened.

beats.caption: Caracol Altar 21, dedicated in AD 633, records a "star war" defeat of the Holy Lord of Tikal.
The attacker's name is damaged; Martin finds no basis for Caracol's king and suggests the Snake kingdom.
The defeat coincides with the start of a roughly 130-year lacuna in monument dedications at Tikal.
